summary: Initial knowledge from the root README: purpose, roles, architecture, scheduled jobs, UI pages, data notes, security, backups, deployment.

ops.text: KitchenHQ is an AI sous-chef for the household: it plans the week's meals, batches prep, keeps the pantry accurate and writes the shopping list, automatically on a schedule or on demand from a chat window.
ops.quote: plans your week's meals, batches your prep, keeps your pantry honest, and writes your shopping list

ops.text: KitchenHQ is a small, self-hostable stack of three services run with one `docker compose up`.
ops.quote: small, self-hostable stack of three services you run with one `docker compose up`

ops.text: In KitchenHQ a team of LLM agents does the thinking, a SQLite database is the single source of truth, and a React UI is how the household steers it.
ops.quote: A team of LLM agents does the thinking; a SQLite database is the single source of truth

ops.text: KitchenHQ has four specialist agent roles: Executive Chef, Sous Chef, Pantry Manager and Food Inspector.
ops.quote: Executive Chef (weekly menu), Sous Chef (prep & cooking plans), Pantry Manager (shopping), Food Inspector

ops.text: KitchenHQ is self-contained: pinned dependencies, SQLite with online backups, and no cloud services required (bring your own OpenAI key, or run Ollama locally).
ops.quote: Pinned dependencies, SQLite with online backups, no cloud services required

ops.text: KitchenHQ exists to turn the recurring daily household feeding logistics (what to eat, what to defrost, what is about to run out, what goes on the list) into a set of background jobs and a conversation.
ops.quote: KitchenHQ turns that recurring load into a set of background jobs and a conversation

ops.text: The Executive Chef reads the inventory and household preferences and writes a full Monday-Sunday menu covering breakfast, lunch, snack and dinner.
ops.quote: reads your inventory and household preferences and writes a full Monday–Sunday menu

ops.text: The Executive Chef searches the household's own recipe catalog for a match before inventing a dish.
ops.quote: searching your own recipe catalog for a match before inventing anything

ops.text: Menu planning respects the household's dietary rules and prep-time caps.
ops.quote: respecting your dietary rules and prep-time caps

ops.text: Nightly and morning jobs turn each day's menu into an ordered, time-capped prep checklist and a parallel cooking plan.
ops.quote: turn each day's menu into an ordered, time-capped prep checklist and a parallel cooking plan

ops.text: Completing a prep task deducts exactly what it used from inventory.
ops.quote: Completing a prep task deducts exactly what it used from inventory

ops.text: When stock dips below its threshold, the Pantry Manager drafts a shopping list that is merged and de-duplicated.
ops.quote: When stock dips below its threshold, the Pantry Manager drafts a shopping list

ops.text: The Food Inspector never plans anything; it scores every menu slot, weekly plan, prep task and recipe saved by the other three roles against the household's own rules and leaves a written reason.
ops.quote: it scores every menu slot, weekly plan, prep task, and recipe the other three save, against the household's own rules, and leaves a written reason

ops.text: Food Inspector scoring uses the household's own configurable rules, never a hardcoded checker.
ops.quote: against your household's own configurable rules — never a hardcoded checker

ops.text: Chat with the chef supports swaps, substitutions and "what can I make with what's in the fridge" requests, with full conversation history persisted and resumable.
ops.quote: full conversation history, persisted, resumable

ops.text: Email notifications are opt-in via SMTP: the agents can email the weekly plan, tonight's prep or the shopping list to the address on the Profile page.
ops.quote: Opt-in SMTP: the agents email you the weekly plan, tonight's prep, or the shopping list

ops.text: Email is never sent automatically: a job asks for an email as one of its steps.
ops.quote: There is **no** automatic send: a job asks for an email as one of its steps

ops.text: A disabled notification toggle or an unset `SMTP_HOST` returns `{"sent": false}` and does not fail the job.
ops.quote: a disabled toggle or unset host simply comes back as `{"sent": false}` without failing the job

ops.text: If a job stops short of its required DB writes, `run_agent` sends corrective nudges and then raises, so a job that saved 22 of 28 menu slots is recorded `failed` with the shortfall, never a blank `completed`.
ops.quote: a job that saved 22 of 28 menu slots is recorded `failed` with the shortfall, never a blank `completed`

ops.text: The Executive Chef owns the weekly menu (28 slots with full recipes and macros, described in household-facing language); its structured output `ExecutiveChefResult` is used for the weekly-menu job only.
ops.quote: The weekly menu — 28 slots, full recipes, macros, described in household-facing language

ops.text: The Executive Chef owns the recipe catalog from chat (add / find / update / rate a recipe), and chat with the chef stays free-text.
ops.quote: owns that catalog from chat (add / find / update / rate a recipe). Chat with the chef stays free-text.

ops.text: The Sous Chef owns prep schedules and parallel cooking plans, each capped in minutes, and records exactly what each task will consume so inventory can deduct on completion; its structured output is `SousChefResult`.
ops.quote: Records exactly what each task will consume so inventory can deduct on completion

ops.text: The Pantry Manager owns the pending shopping list (what is below threshold or short for the week), upserted so add-vs-append is never a choice; its structured output is `PantryManagerResult`.
ops.quote: upserted so add-vs-append is never a choice

ops.text: The Food Inspector audits what the other three roles already saved (menu slots, whole-week plans, prep tasks, recipes) and records a 0-100 score plus written feedback on each; its structured output is `FoodInspectorResult`.
ops.quote: records a 0–100 score plus written feedback on each

ops.text: The Food Inspector is scheduled/automation-only and has no chat persona.
ops.quote: Scheduled/automation-only, no chat persona

ops.text: KitchenHQ consists of three independently deployable services orchestrated by the root `docker-compose.yml`: dbmcp, agent-api and chatui.
ops.quote: Three independently deployable services, orchestrated by the root `docker-compose.yml`

ops.text: Backend stack: Python 3, FastAPI, FastMCP / `mcp`, LangChain 1.x, `langchain-mcp-adapters`, `langchain-openai` / `langchain-ollama`, APScheduler, SQLite.
ops.quote: **Backend:** Python 3, FastAPI, FastMCP / `mcp`, LangChain 1.x

ops.text: Frontend stack: React 18, Vite, `lucide-react`.
ops.quote: **Frontend:** React 18, Vite, `lucide-react`.

ops.text: Infrastructure: Docker Compose, with pinned dependencies throughout.
ops.quote: **Infra:** Docker Compose, pinned dependencies throughout.

ops.text: dbmcp (dir `dbmcp/`) is a Python FastAPI + FastMCP service on port 18000 that owns the SQLite database (`kitchen.db`) and its schema.
ops.quote: Owns the SQLite database and its schema/migrations

ops.text: dbmcp exposes every data operation twice, as REST (`/api/*`) and as MCP tools (`/mcp`), from one FastAPI app.
ops.quote: Exposes every data operation twice — as REST (`/api/*`) and as MCP tools (`/mcp`) — from one FastAPI app

ops.text: agent-api (dir `agents/`) is a Python LangChain + APScheduler service on port 8090.
ops.quote: | **agent-api** | `agents/` | Python · LangChain · APScheduler | 8090 |

ops.text: agent-api is the only process that talks to the LLM and to dbmcp over MCP.
ops.quote: The only process that talks to the LLM and to `dbmcp` over MCP

ops.text: agent-api serves `/chat` and `/invoke/{job}` and runs the cron jobs in-process.
ops.quote: Serves `/chat` and `/invoke/{job}`, and runs the cron jobs in-process

ops.text: Every agent-api request builds and disposes its own LLM/MCP connections; nothing outlives a single call.
ops.quote: Every request builds and disposes its own LLM/MCP connections — nothing outlives a single call

ops.text: chatui (dir `chatui/`) is a React (Vite) single-page app served on port 8080 by a thin FastAPI backend.
ops.quote: React SPA served by a thin FastAPI backend

ops.text: chatui proxies CRUD calls to dbmcp and chat/automation calls to agent-api.
ops.quote: proxies CRUD to `dbmcp` and chat/automation calls to `agent-api`

ops.text: chatui holds no LangChain/MCP dependency and is a pure REST client.
ops.quote: **chatui** is a pure REST client

ops.text: chatui calls dbmcp directly for all CRUD/read data (`/api/dashboard` and friends) and agent-api for anything that needs the LLM (chat, "run job now").
ops.quote: It calls **dbmcp** directly for all CRUD/read data

ops.text: agent-api reaches dbmcp over MCP (`/mcp`) for every data operation the agent performs.
ops.quote: reaches **dbmcp** over **MCP** (`/mcp`) for every data operation the agent performs

ops.text: The only REST calls agent-api makes to dbmcp are inside the email tools: fetching the recipient address and back-filling the saved menu / pending shopping list so the model's tool call can stay minimal.
ops.quote: The only REST calls it makes to dbmcp are inside the email tools

ops.text: Each agent run's toolset is the remote MCP tools from dbmcp plus local in-process tools: `get_job_context` and the three `send_*_email` tools.
ops.quote: **remote MCP tools** (from dbmcp) + **local in-process tools**

ops.text: The three `send_*_email` tools talk SMTP directly to the mail server; when disabled they are a harmless no-op.
ops.quote: which talk SMTP directly to your mail server; disabled = harmless no-op

ops.text: The LLM provider is either OpenAI (`OPENAI_API_KEY`) or a local Ollama (`LLM_PROVIDER=ollama` plus `OLLAMA_BASE_URL`).
ops.quote: either an OpenAI API key or a local Ollama

ops.text: Optional email uses an SMTP server configured via `SMTP_HOST` (and credentials) in the root `.env`; a Gmail app password works (`smtp.gmail.com:587`).
ops.quote: A Gmail app password works (`smtp.gmail.com:587`)

ops.text: Bounded connection lifetime: agent-api builds a fresh LLM client and MCP toolset per request and disposes them in a `finally` block; there is no long-lived agent object and no cross-call lock, so concurrent chats and jobs run fully independently.
ops.quote: There is no long-lived agent object and no cross-call lock; concurrent chats and jobs run fully independently

ops.text: The bounded-connection-lifetime design is a deliberate fix for a real incident where a stale long-lived Ollama connection wedged the host.
ops.quote: a real incident where a stale long-lived Ollama connection wedged the host

ops.text: The cron scheduler runs in-process on an `AsyncIOScheduler` inside the agent-api process, with no extra worker container and no network hop.
ops.quote: on an `AsyncIOScheduler` inside the API process — no extra worker container, no network hop

ops.text: Role boundaries are enforced by the prompt, not by hiding tools: all four roles get the identical MCP toolset.
ops.quote: role boundaries are enforced by the prompt, not by hiding tools

ops.text: The weekly menu has no deterministic policy check: `user_profile.restrictions` is the only rule source.
ops.quote: The weekly menu has no deterministic policy check

ops.text: The Executive Chef reads the restrictions via `get_household_preferences` while planning, and the Food Inspector reads the same thing while auditing (`menu_audit` for per-meal rules, `weekly_plan_audit` for week-scope rules such as lunch variety).
ops.quote: the Food Inspector reads the same thing while auditing

ops.text: There is no synchronous gate before a plan is saved or emailed.
ops.quote: there is no synchronous gate before a plan is saved or emailed

ops.text: Prep deduction deliberately does not guard on stock: a deduction always applies and can leave a visible negative balance until a shopping run.
ops.quote: This is intentional.

ops.text: `dbmcp/schema.sql` is the single source of truth for the schema: a fresh-start `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` script with no in-place migration of older layouts.
ops.quote: a fresh-start `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` script with no in-place migration of older layouts

ops.text: `dbmcp/db_design.md` documents the same schema for humans; if it disagrees with `schema.sql`, `schema.sql` wins.
ops.quote: if the two disagree, `schema.sql` wins

ops.text: Data operations are plain functions in `kitchendb/tools/*.py`, added once to a `FastMCP` instance (`/mcp`) and re-exposed as thin REST routes (`/api/*`) from the same FastAPI app.
ops.quote: holds the data operations as plain functions, added once to a `FastMCP` instance

ops.text: Inventory writes are propose-then-acknowledge: the propose step never touches `inventory`, and the acknowledge step is idempotent via a required `acknowledgement_key`.
ops.quote: The propose step never touches `inventory`; the acknowledge step is idempotent via a required `acknowledgement_key`

ops.text: There is no "shopping list" entity: `shopping_items` is the one pending list, unique on `item_name`.
ops.quote: `shopping_items` *is* the one pending list, unique on `item_name`

ops.text: `add_shopping_items` is an upsert.
ops.quote: `add_shopping_items` is an upsert

ops.text: Acknowledging a shopping purchase adds the real quantity to `inventory` and deletes the `shopping_items` row.
ops.quote: acknowledging a purchase adds the real quantity to `inventory` and deletes the row

ops.text: `user_profile.restrictions` is household-editable on the Profile page, and each entry is scoped `per_meal` or `week`.
ops.quote: household-editable on the Profile page; each entry scoped `per_meal` or `week`

ops.text: A `recipes` row holds the structured recipe, its embedding and its rating together.
ops.quote: A `recipes` row holds the structured recipe, its embedding, and a rating together

ops.text: `add_recipe` / `update_recipe` recompute the embedding synchronously, so `search_recipes` can never search a stale vector.
ops.quote: recompute the embedding synchronously

ops.text: `search_recipes` is a hybrid keyword + semantic search with no external vector store.
ops.quote: hybrid keyword + semantic, no external vector store

ops.text: Prompts live in `agents/prompts/*.md`; `system.md` is a role-neutral shared base (household context, dietary rules) and each role fragment is appended as "Your role".
ops.quote: `system.md` is a role-neutral shared base (household context, dietary rules); each role fragment is appended as "Your role"

ops.text: Job-specific detail (which day, which meals, the time cap) lives in `agents/app/jobs.py`, not in the prompts.
ops.quote: lives separately in `agents/app/jobs.py`, not the prompts

ops.text: Each agent run gets a locally-built `get_job_context` tool, the authoritative source for date math and the intent behind a scheduled run.
ops.quote: the authoritative source for date math and the *intent* behind a scheduled run

ops.text: agent-api fires eleven cron jobs in-process, defined in `agents/app/scheduler.py`.
ops.quote: Eleven cron jobs fire in-process (`agents/app/scheduler.py`)

ops.text: Cron job times are interpreted in `KITCHEN_TIMEZONE` (default `Asia/Kolkata`).
ops.quote: Times are in `KITCHEN_TIMEZONE` (default `Asia/Kolkata`)

ops.text: Every scheduled job is also `POST /invoke/{job_name}` and can be triggered from the Automations page to see its output immediately.
ops.quote: Every one is also a `POST /invoke/{job_name}` you can trigger from the **Automations** page

ops.text: Job `weekly_menu` (Executive Chef) runs Saturday 10:00 and replaces the saved menu with a fresh, complete Mon-Sun week.
ops.quote: | `weekly_menu` | Executive Chef | Sat 10:00 |

ops.text: Job `sunday_prep` (Sous Chef) runs Sunday 14:00 and produces one 60-minute batch-prep session for the week ahead.
ops.quote: | `sunday_prep` | Sous Chef | Sun 14:00 |

ops.text: Job `nightly_prep` (Sous Chef) runs daily at 20:00 and creates a task of at most 10 minutes tonight so tomorrow's breakfast and lunch are quick.
ops.quote: | `nightly_prep` | Sous Chef | daily 20:00 |

ops.text: Job `morning_cooking` (Sous Chef) runs Mon-Fri 06:30 and produces a parallel cooking plan for the breakfast and lunch being made now.
ops.quote: | `morning_cooking` | Sous Chef | Mon–Fri 06:30 |

ops.text: Job `dinner_cooking` (Sous Chef) runs Mon-Fri 18:00 and produces a parallel cooking plan for tonight's snack and dinner.
ops.quote: | `dinner_cooking` | Sous Chef | Mon–Fri 18:00 |

ops.text: Job `pantry_manager` (Pantry Manager) runs daily at 18:00 and proposes a shopping list for whatever is running low or needed for the week.
ops.quote: | `pantry_manager` | Pantry Manager | daily 18:00 |

ops.text: Job `expire_prep_tasks` (role Sous Chef) runs every 2 hours as deterministic housekeeping, flipping any prep task nobody acted on within 2 hours to `expired`.
ops.quote: | `expire_prep_tasks` | Sous Chef | every 2 hours |

ops.text: Job `menu_audit` (Food Inspector) runs daily at 22:30 and scores every unaudited weekly-menu slot against household rules and preferences.
ops.quote: | `menu_audit` | Food Inspector | daily 22:30 |

ops.text: Job `weekly_plan_audit` (Food Inspector) runs daily at 22:35 and scores whole-week completeness and week-scope rules (e.g. lunch variety) against the context that week was actually planned under.
ops.quote: | `weekly_plan_audit` | Food Inspector | daily 22:35 |

ops.text: Job `task_audit` (Food Inspector) runs daily at 22:45 and scores every unaudited prep task, including cancelled ones (the decision is judged, not whether it happened).
ops.quote: | `task_audit` | Food Inspector | daily 22:45 |

ops.text: Job `recipe_audit` (Food Inspector) runs daily at 23:00 and scores every unaudited catalog recipe against recipe-catalog standards only (tags, instruction quality), independent of any household's preferences.
ops.quote: | `recipe_audit` | Food Inspector | daily 23:00 |

ops.text: agent-api can be run standalone with `pip install -r requirements.txt` in `agents/`, then `python -m uvicorn app.server:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8090` for the API plus scheduler.
ops.quote: python -m uvicorn app.server:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8090

ops.text: `python cli.py` in `agents/` gives an interactive terminal REPL with the Executive Chef, with no server.
ops.quote: or: interactive terminal REPL with the Executive Chef, no server

ops.text: dbmcp can be run standalone: `pip install -r requirements.txt`, then `KITCHENHQ_API_KEY=... python init_db.py`, which creates/seeds `kitchen.db` on startup and serves REST + MCP on port 18000.
ops.quote: creates/seeds kitchen.db on startup, serves REST + MCP on :18000

ops.text: chatui can be run standalone with `npm install` and `npm run dev` (Vite dev server), or `npm run build && python -m uvicorn app:app --port 8080` to serve the built app from FastAPI.
ops.quote: npm run build && python -m uvicorn app:app --port 8080

ops.text: chatui is one React app with no router; `App.jsx` switch-renders each page.
ops.quote: One React app, no router

ops.text: The Dashboard page shows the week at a glance: today's meals, open tasks and the low-stock count.
ops.quote: the week at a glance: today's meals, open tasks, low-stock count

ops.text: The Weekly Menu page shows every slot with ingredients and full recipe, plus its Food Inspector score/feedback badge.
ops.quote: every slot with ingredients and full recipe, plus its Food Inspector score/feedback badge

ops.text: The Recipes page is the household's searchable catalog: a recipe can be rated, or the Executive Chef can be asked in one click to refresh its tags or rewrite its instructions, with the Food Inspector's own feedback fed in as context.
ops.quote: feeding it the Food Inspector's own feedback as context

ops.text: The Pantry page is a read-only inventory view with thresholds and last-updated.
ops.quote: read-only inventory with thresholds and last-updated

ops.text: The Tasks page shows prep schedules; checking one complete deducts its ingredients from inventory, and tasks are also scored by the Food Inspector.
ops.quote: checking one complete deducts its ingredients from inventory

ops.text: The Chat page talks to the Executive Chef and can list and resume the 5 most recent conversations.
ops.quote: list and resume the 5 most recent conversations

ops.text: The Automations page lists every scheduled job with its recent runs and a "run now" button per job.
ops.quote: every scheduled job, its recent runs, and a "run now" button per job

ops.text: The Usage Stats page shows daily and all-time token/context usage broken down per agent role.
ops.quote: daily and all-time token/context usage, broken down per agent role

ops.text: The Profile page edits the single household record: name (drives the greeting), email (where notifications go), notification toggle, household members, restrictions and chef notes.
ops.quote: the single household record: name (drives the greeting)

ops.text: Every scheduled run is recorded with its tool calls, output, token usage and success/failure.
ops.quote: Every scheduled run is recorded with its tool calls, output, token usage, and success/failure

ops.text: Telemetry for every run (success or failure), including token/context usage, is posted to dbmcp and visible on the Usage Stats page.
ops.quote: is posted to `dbmcp` and visible on the **Usage Stats** page

ops.text: A single shared secret, `KITCHENHQ_API_KEY`, gates every REST and MCP request across all three services.
ops.quote: A single shared secret gates every REST and MCP request across all three services

ops.text: A `require_api_key` middleware sits in front of every route except `/api/health` on dbmcp and chatui, checking `X-API-Key` against `KITCHENHQ_API_KEY`.
ops.quote: checking `X-API-Key` against `KITCHENHQ_API_KEY`

ops.text: On dbmcp the middleware is outer FastAPI middleware, so it also covers the mounted MCP app at `/mcp`; there is no separate MCP-layer auth.
ops.quote: no separate MCP-layer auth

ops.text: The browser prompts for `KITCHENHQ_API_KEY`, stores it in `localStorage` and sends it as `X-API-Key` on every request.
ops.quote: stored in `localStorage`, sent as `X-API-Key` on every request

ops.text: The shared key can be generated with `python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))"`.
ops.quote: secrets.token_urlsafe(32)

ops.text: Authentication is one shared key for the whole household, not per-user accounts.
ops.quote: One shared key for the whole household (not per-user accounts)

ops.text: KitchenHQ is described as prototype-grade: it runs a family kitchen well but is not hardened for the open internet.
ops.quote: **This is prototype-grade.**

ops.text: `python dbmcp/scripts/backup_db.py` takes an online-backup snapshot of the database into `dbmcp/backups/`, keeping the last 14.
ops.quote: online-backup snapshot into dbmcp/backups/, keeps last 14

ops.text: The backup script is safe under concurrent writers because it uses the SQLite online-backup API.
ops.quote: Safe under concurrent writers (SQLite online-backup API)

ops.text: The README advises scheduling the backup script daily via cron / Task Scheduler.
ops.quote: Schedule it daily via cron / Task Scheduler

ops.text: SQLite has no replication; only local timestamped snapshots exist.
ops.quote: SQLite with no replication (only local timestamped snapshots)

ops.text: There is no CI, and linting/formatting is not configured.
ops.quote: no CI; linting/formatting not configured

ops.text: Automated tests exist for dbmcp only (`cd dbmcp && pip install -r requirements-dev.txt && pytest tests/`); each test spins up a temp SQLite DB and needs no live server.
ops.quote: each test spins up a temp SQLite DB, no live server needed

ops.text: chatui and agents have no automated tests yet.
ops.quote: `chatui` and `agents` have no automated tests yet

ops.text: Prerequisites are Docker + Docker Compose and either an OpenAI API key or a local Ollama.
ops.quote: **Prerequisites:** Docker + Docker Compose, and either an OpenAI API key or a local Ollama

ops.text: Setup: copy `.env.example` to `.env` and set `KITCHENHQ_API_KEY` (the shared secret for all three services).
ops.quote: Root env — shared secret for all three services

ops.text: Setup: copy `agents/.env.example` to `agents/.env`, set `OPENAI_API_KEY` (or `LLM_PROVIDER=ollama` + `OLLAMA_BASE_URL`) and the same `KITCHENHQ_API_KEY`.
ops.quote: set the same KITCHENHQ_API_KEY value

ops.text: The whole stack is started from the repo root with `docker compose up --build`, and the UI is then at http://localhost:8080.
ops.quote: Then open **http://localhost:8080**

ops.text: A subset of services can be run while iterating, e.g. `docker compose up --build dbmcp chatui`.
ops.quote: Run a subset while iterating

ops.text: The README architecture diagram labels agent-api "6 cron jobs, in-process", while the rest of the README lists and counts 11 cron jobs; the diagram is presumed stale and needs confirmation.
ops.quote: (6 cron jobs, in-process)
